hub: ^Sterling's still in the building. How do I play this?
^Send me the RFID cloning field guide
^Send me the distcc exploitation field guide
^Send me the CyberChef decoding field guide
hint_confrontation: ^Agent HaX: Listen carefully. You've got the logs. The case stands whether or not she's in cuffs.
^Agent HaX: Want the Architect? Offer her a deal, and a cold one. She flips to save herself, not because she's sorry -- don't mistake the two.
^Agent HaX: Want her off the board? Arrest her. But she came ready to run, so corner her or she walks.
^Agent HaX: And if the evidence is enough for you, let her go and secure it. Your call. None of them are clean.

b: ^Agent HaX: If it's the deal you want, bring her something she can't shrug off. The drive in her desk.

request_rfid_guide: ^Agent HaX: Read, crack, emulate. Reception's card is weak defaults, so a dictionary attack is near instant. Sterling's is custom keys, so run Darkside once you've read it. About half a minute.
request_recon_guide: ^Agent HaX: Map before you touch anything. nmap the subnet, read the versions, then pick your target. The scan flag comes off a clean sweep.
request_proftpd_guide: ^Agent HaX: ProFTPD guide sent. That's the backdoor that took St. Catherine's down.
^Agent HaX: Their FTP box runs the trojaned 1.3.3c build. Anonymous login gets you nothing that matters; the backdoor gets you root.
request_cyberchef_guide: ^Agent HaX: ROT13, Base64, hex. If a decode still looks scrambled, it's layered -- decode again. There's no key to find; encoding isn't encryption.
request_lockpicking_guide: ^Agent HaX: Light tension, find the binding pin, set it, repeat -- and only once he's passed the door and turned away from it. Pick in his sightline and you're made.
request_netexploit_guide: ^Agent HaX: The legacy distcc daemon on 3632 runs jobs for anyone who asks -- CVE-2004-2687. Point the distcc_exec module at it and the operational logs are yours.
hint_rfid: ^Agent HaX: Two stages. Reception first -- lean in near her desk and the cloner picks the MIFARE signal off her lanyard. Weak defaults, so read it, run a dictionary attack, save it, and it opens the conference door.
^Agent HaX: Then Sterling's executive card in the meeting. Custom keys, so read it, then run Darkside, about half a minute. Best moment is when you're both at the whiteboard. Keep her talking.

c-0: ^Agent HaX: That order every time. The server room won't open until you emulate her cracked card at the door.

hint_lockpicking: ^Agent HaX: You've got the pick kit from the start. Sterling's office and the cabinets are keyed -- approach a locked one and interact.
^Agent HaX: It takes time and it exposes you. Watch the guard's loop and only work the lock when his back's turned. If he catches you at it, that's a detection you don't get back.
hint_password: ^Agent HaX: People never change the default. That IT slip on her monitor tells you the format.
^Agent HaX: The founding year's on the plaque in reception. Put the two together.
^Agent HaX: The wall safe's a different code. She mails it to the night team from her office. Check what's sitting on her machine unsent.
hint_encoding: ^Agent HaX: Take the laptop in the server room -- it's loaded with CyberChef. Paste anything that looks like nonsense.
^Agent HaX: ROT13 reads like scrambled English. Base64 is letters, numbers, plus and slash. Hex is pairs of 0-9 and A-F.
^Agent HaX: And if it's still scrambled after one pass, it's layered. Decode again. The drive in her desk is Base64 over ROT13 -- two passes.
hint_network: ^Agent HaX: The VM terminal in the server room reaches 192.168.100.0/24. Scan first, then work the services.

^Agent HaX: The FTP box is the ProFTPD backdoor you met at St. Catherine's; the web host has the price list. distcc is the one that matters -- that's where the operational logs are. Submit all four at the drop-site.

b: ^Agent HaX: Day one still. Get Sterling's card cloned -- everything after that depends on server room access.
^Agent HaX: Network's stripped and the case is made. Sterling's your last move. Take Danny Foster's office first if you want a say in his end.
^Agent HaX: And her desk drawer's still got that drive in it, if you want something to bargain with.

report_progress: ^Agent HaX: You're in after hours. Status:

b: ^Agent HaX: Recon, FTP and pricing flags are in. Just distcc left -- that's the logs, that's the case.
^Agent HaX: Flags going in. Keep working the services. The distcc box is the one that finishes it.
^Agent HaX: And the guard hasn't so much as looked at you. Stay that way.
^Agent HaX: The guard's clocked you at least once. Tighten up -- pick locks only when he's turned away.

c-0: ^Agent HaX: Call if you need me.

on_rfid_clone_success: ^Agent HaX: Crack complete. Sterling's card is in the cloner.
^Agent HaX: Sit tight until the place clears out, then the server room door. Emulate her card there. That's when the real work starts.
on_victoria_computer_accessed: ^Agent HaX: You're into her machine. Good.
^Agent HaX: Client roster, transaction records, anything to the Architect.

b: ^Agent HaX: And that board in the server room said she mails the night team from in there. Anything she hasn't sent yet is worth a look.

m2_revelation_call: ^, I've got the distcc logs you just submitted.
^Agent HaX: There it is. The ProFTPD backdoor. Line item on invoice ZDS-2024-0847: twenty-five thousand, priced in US dollars like everything else on that market, part of a package to Ghost.
^Agent HaX: Target line: St. Catherine's Regional. Sable's sign-off on the approval.
^Agent HaX: This is the thing we couldn't prove at the hospital. Zero Day armed Ghost. It's on the record now, timestamped and attributed.

c-0: ^You: Direct chain. Zero Day to Ghost to St. Catherine's. That stands up.
^Agent HaX: It does. ENTROPY procurement, in writing. Ironclad.
c-1: ^You: They charged extra to attack a hospital. That's not negligence, that's a pricing decision.
^Agent HaX: That's the line a jury remembers. Keep it.
c-2: ^You: If they invoice one cell like this, they invoice all of them.
^Agent HaX: Which is the whole reason you're in there. Finish it.

m2_revelation_impact: ^Agent HaX: Pull the rest while you're standing in it. The catalogue, the roster, the drive in her desk. Every page is another cell we can name.
^ -- the logs point at a Phase 2. Bigger than a hospital. If you find the directive, we get ahead of it for once.

c-0: ^Agent HaX: I know you will. Go.
c-1: ^Agent HaX: One page at a time. Starting tonight.

m2_revelation_end: ^Agent HaX: Finish up, then Sterling. And be careful -- reasonable as she sounds, she signed that invoice.
on_exploit_catalog_found: ^Agent HaX: The catalogue. Every exploit they sell, with a price and a premium.
^Agent HaX: The ProFTPD line names Ghost and St. Catherine's outright. That's the sale, in their own filing.
on_architect_directive_found: ^Agent HaX: That drive from her desk. Run it through the laptop and tell me what it says.
^Agent HaX: If it's what I think, it's the Architect talking. We take it to Command tonight.
on_victoria_ko_card: ^Agent HaX: Well. That's one way to end a job interview.
^Agent HaX: If her card's come loose, leave it where it fell -- it's evidence. Nightshade has lifted its keys from the reader logs and built you a working copy.
^Agent HaX: It's in your kit now. It opens what hers opens, which means the server room tonight.
